micronarrative: To be totally blunt and honest, the thing that stands out to me first is just how fast social media as a whole can completely distort a local business's day-to-day reality over something so harmless. It's really disheartening to see a simple celebration weaponized like that, but I'll admit the neighborhood that is rallying together with a buy-out day, gives me a whole lot of hope. Living in a world where online outrage spreads like wildfire feels pretty uncomfortable to me, especially seeing people physically show up for one another is always a very nice reminder of actual community spirit, human kindness, and true compassion. Growing up juggling different ways of speaking or switching between groups definitely makes you hyper-aware of how context and tone change everything. You pick up on subtle cues pretty quickly, so when you see people online completely misreading or twisting someone's words, it's pretty frustrating to watch. That hyper-awareness makes it pretty clear how fast a wave of bad-faith twisted reviews can hit a small business right in the wallet.
